records.source: בָּרֲכִ֥י נַפְשִׁ֗י אֶת־יְה֫וָ֥ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהַי גָּדַ֣לְתָּ מְּאֹ֑ד ה֭וֹד וְהָדָ֣ר לָבָֽשְׁתָּ׃
records.gloss: Bless YHWH, my soul. YHWH my God, you are very great; splendor and majesty you have put on,
pieces: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, how great {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are! Splendor and majesty are the robes {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wear,

L.1: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are very great; [with] splendor and majesty {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are clothed,

R.1: With all that I am, I praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are so great! Glory and royal honor are like clothes {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wear.

decisions.choice: a psalm with no title, joined to Psalm 103
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives this psalm no title. It opens and closes with the call that opens and closes Psalm 103 (103:1, 22), and it praises God as the Creator, following much the same order as Genesis 1.
As in 103:1.

decisions.choice: clothed with splendor and majesty: royal glory
decisions.reason: Splendor and majesty (hod, hadar) are the glory of a king (21:6; 45:4); God wears them as clothing (93:1).
Verses 2-4 go on describing God in a series of phrases, so verses 1-3 end with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: With all that I am, I praise the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 103:1.

records.heading: The Creator's world, full of creatures

records.source: עֹֽטֶה־א֭וֹר כַּשַּׂלְמָ֑ה נוֹטֶ֥ה שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם כַּיְרִיעָֽה׃
records.gloss: wrapping [yourself in] light as [in] a garment, stretching out [the] heavens like a curtain,
pieces: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wrap {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} in light as in a cloak and spread out the sky like a tent cloth,

L.2: wrapping {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} in light as [in] a garment, stretching out the heavens like a tent curtain,

R.2: You wear light as if it were a coat. You spread out the sky like a tent.

decisions.choice: light and the heavens: the first works of creation
decisions.reason: Light was made on the first day and the vault of the sky on the second (Genesis 1:3-8). God is pictured putting on light and pitching the sky like a tent (Isaiah 40:22).

decisions.choice: a curtain: the cloth of a tent
decisions.reason: The word (yeri'ah) is a tent curtain, the cloth of the tent itself (Isaiah 54:2).

records.source: הַ֥מְקָרֶֽה בַמַּ֗יִם עֲֽלִיּ֫וֹתָ֥יו הַשָּׂם־עָבִ֥ים רְכוּב֑וֹ הַֽ֝מְהַלֵּ֗ךְ עַל־כַּנְפֵי־רֽוּחַ׃
records.gloss: the [one who] lays the beams of his upper rooms in the waters, the [one who] makes clouds his chariot, the [one who] walks on [the] wings of [the] wind,
pieces: who builds {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} upper rooms with beams set in the waters above, who turns the clouds into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chariot and travels on the wings of the wind,

L.3: who lays the beams of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} upper rooms in the waters, who makes clouds {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chariot, who walks on the wings of the wind,

R.3: He built {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home high above, on the waters over the sky. He uses the clouds as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chariot. He travels on the wings of the wind.

decisions.choice: upper rooms on the waters: God's house above the sky
decisions.reason: The sky was pictured as holding back waters above it (Genesis 1:7; 148:4). God's upper rooms, like the cool rooms on a roof, are built on those waters.

decisions.choice: his: from speaking to God to speaking of him
decisions.reason: Verses 1-2 speak to God; from here the psalm often speaks about him, and turns to him again in verses 6-9, 13, 20 and 24-30.

decisions.choice: the wings of the wind: the swift wind
decisions.reason: The wind is pictured with wings, carrying God as he moves through his world (18:11).
Readable says where these waters are (m1).

records.source: עֹשֶׂ֣ה מַלְאָכָ֣יו רוּח֑וֹת מְ֝שָׁרְתָ֗יו אֵ֣שׁ לֹהֵֽט׃
records.gloss: making his messengers winds, his servants a fire blazing.
pieces: who makes the winds {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} messengers and flames of fire {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants.

L.4: making {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} messengers winds, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants a blazing fire.

R.4: He sends out the winds as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} messengers. Blazing fire serves {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be read either way: God makes winds and fire serve him, or he makes his messengers (angels) into winds and fire. The verses around speak of wind, cloud and fire in God's service, which favors the first reading. Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

Hebrews 1:7 quotes this verse from the ancient Greek translation, "he makes his angels winds (or spirits)", to show that angels serve while the Son reigns. The Hebrew word (mal'akh) means both messenger and angel.
Fire here may be lightning, which goes out at God's command (148:8).

records.source: יָֽסַד־אֶ֭רֶץ עַל־מְכוֹנֶ֑יהָ בַּל־תִּ֝מּ֗וֹט עוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃
records.gloss: He established [the] earth on its foundations; it will not be shaken forever and ever.
pieces: He fixed the earth on its bases, never to be toppled, for all time to come.

L.5: He founded the earth on its foundations; it will not be shaken forever and ever.

R.5: He built the earth on a strong base. Nothing can ever move it.

decisions.reason: The earth is pictured as a building set on pillars or footings (24:2; 1 Samuel 2:8; Job 38:4-6). It stands because God made it firm (93:1; 96:10).

records.source: תְּ֭הוֹם כַּלְּב֣וּשׁ כִּסִּית֑וֹ עַל־הָ֝רִ֗ים יַֽעַמְדוּ־מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: [The] deep like clothing you covered it; above [the] mountains stood [the] waters.
pieces: The deep was the robe {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put over it; the waters rose and stood above the mountains.

L.6: [With the] deep as [with] clothing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} covered it; above the mountains the waters stood.

R.6: You covered the earth with deep water like a blanket. The water was higher than the mountains.

decisions.choice: the deep over the earth: Genesis 1:2, 9
decisions.reason: At the beginning the deep (tehom) covered everything (Genesis 1:2), until God gathered the waters and dry land appeared (Genesis 1:9). Verses 6-9 tell that story.
"It" is the earth of verse 5: God wrapped it in the deep like a garment.
Readable names what "it" refers to (m2).

records.source: מִן־גַּעֲרָ֣תְךָ֣ יְנוּס֑וּן מִן־ק֥וֹל רַֽ֝עַמְךָ֗ יֵחָפֵזֽוּן׃
records.gloss: From your rebuke they fled; from [the] sound of your thunder they hurried away,
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rebuked them, the waters ran; at the roar of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} thunder they rushed off,

L.7: From {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rebuke they fled; from the sound of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} thunder they rushed away,

R.7: You shouted at the waters, and they ran away. When they heard {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} thunder, they hurried off.

decisions.reason: God's rebuke (ge'arah) is the shout that drives back the waters (18:16; 106:9; Job 26:11).
Thunder is the voice of God (29:3; 77:19).
Balanced and Readable name the subject (verse 6).

records.source: יַעֲל֣וּ הָ֭רִים יֵרְד֣וּ בְקָע֑וֹת אֶל־מְ֝ק֗וֹם זֶ֤ה׀יָסַ֬דְתָּ לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: they went up [the] mountains, they went down [the] valleys, to [the] place which you founded for them.
pieces: they went up over the mountains and down into the valleys, to the place {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had fixed for them.

L.8: they went up [the] mountains, they went down [the] valleys, to the place that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} founded for them.

R.8: The water ran over the mountains and down into the valleys, to the place {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made for it.

decisions.choice: the waters went up the mountains and down the valleys
alternatives: the mountains rose, the valleys sank down
decisions.reason: The words can mean that the waters, fleeing, went up over the mountains and down the valleys to their place, or that the mountains rose and the valleys sank as the land appeared. "They" in verses 7 and 9 is the waters, so the first reading is followed here.

decisions.choice: the place you founded for them: the seas
decisions.reason: God gave the waters their own place, the seas (Genesis 1:9-10).

records.source: גְּֽבוּל־שַׂ֭מְתָּ בַּל־יַֽעֲבֹר֑וּן בַּל־יְ֝שׁוּב֗וּן לְכַסּ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: A boundary you set; they will not cross over; they will not return to cover the earth.
pieces: You fixed a limit they may not pass; they will not come back to cover the land.

L.9: A boundary {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set [that] they will not cross; they will not return to cover the earth.

R.9: You marked a line the water cannot cross. It will never again flood the whole earth.

decisions.reason: God set limits for the sea (Job 38:8-11; Proverbs 8:29; Jeremiah 5:22), and promised never again to cover the earth with a flood (Genesis 9:11).

records.source: הַֽמְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ מַ֭עְיָנִים בַּנְּחָלִ֑ים בֵּ֥ין הָ֝רִ֗ים יְהַלֵּכֽוּן׃
records.gloss: the [one who] sends springs into the valleys; between [the] mountains they go.
pieces: You let springs loose into the stream beds; they find their way between the mountains.

L.10: [You are] the one who sends springs into the valleys; between the mountains they flow.

R.10: You make springs of water flow into the valleys. The water runs down between the hills.

decisions.reason: The word (nachal) is a valley with a stream, often dry except in the rainy season.

decisions.choice: the one who sends: God, spoken to
decisions.reason: The verb is a participle with no stated person. Coming after verse 9, it is taken as still speaking to God.
The levels supply the subject (m2); Literal brackets it.

records.source: יַ֭שְׁקוּ כָּל־חַיְת֣וֹ שָׂדָ֑י יִשְׁבְּר֖וּ פְרָאִ֣ים צְמָאָֽם׃
records.gloss: They give drink to every animal of [the] field; wild donkeys break their thirst.
pieces: Every creature of the open country drinks from them; there the wild donkeys satisfy their thirst.

L.11: They give drink to every animal of the field; wild donkeys break their thirst.

R.11: All the wild animals drink from them. Even the wild donkeys find water to drink there.

decisions.choice: every animal of the field: the wild animals
decisions.reason: "The field" is the open country, so these are the wild animals, as against the cattle of verse 14.

decisions.choice: wild donkeys: animals of the desert
decisions.reason: The wild donkey lives free in the dry country (Job 39:5-8); even it finds water.

decisions.choice: break their thirst: quench their thirst
decisions.reason: To break thirst is to end it by drinking.

records.source: עֲ֭לֵיהֶם עוֹף־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם יִשְׁכּ֑וֹן מִבֵּ֥ין עֳ֝פָאיִ֗ם יִתְּנוּ־קֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: Beside them [the] birds of the heavens dwell; from among [the] branches they give voice.
pieces: Close by them the birds of the air settle and call out from the leafy branches.

L.12: By them the birds of the heavens dwell; from among the leaves they lift [their] voice.

R.12: Birds build their nests near the streams. They sing from the branches of the trees.

decisions.reason: The word ('ofa'im) occurs only here; it means the leafy branches of trees.
Readable says what the birds do there.

records.source: מַשְׁקֶ֣ה הָ֭רִים מֵעֲלִיּוֹתָ֑יו מִפְּרִ֥י מַ֝עֲשֶׂ֗יךָ תִּשְׂבַּ֥ע הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Watering [the] mountains from his upper rooms; from [the] fruit of your works the earth is satisfied.
pieces: From {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rooms on high {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} waters the mountains, and the earth has its fill of the fruit of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} work.

L.13: Watering the mountains from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} upper rooms, from the fruit of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works the earth is satisfied.

R.13: From {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home above, God sends rain on the mountains. The earth is filled with the good things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made.

decisions.choice: watering from his upper rooms: rain
decisions.reason: Rain comes down from the waters above the sky, where God's upper rooms are built (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the fruit of your works: what God's work brings
decisions.reason: The fruit of God's works may be the rain itself, or the crops and plants that grow because of it (verse 14).

decisions.choice: his, your: speaking of God and to God
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the psalm moves between speaking about God and speaking to him, here within one verse.
Readable names God, who is meant by "his", at the start of the sentence.

records.source: מַצְמִ֤יחַ חָצִ֨יר׀לַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וְ֭עֵשֶׂב לַעֲבֹדַ֣ת הָאָדָ֑ם לְה֥וֹצִיא לֶ֝֗חֶם מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: causing to grow grass for the cattle, and plants for [the] labor of humankind, to bring forth bread from the earth,
pieces: He makes grass spring up for the herds and plants for people to tend, so that food comes out of the ground,

L.14: Causing grass to grow for the cattle, and plants for the labor of humankind, to bring forth bread from the earth,

R.14: He makes grass grow for the cattle. He gives plants for people to grow on their farms, so that they can get food from the ground.

decisions.choice: for the labor of humankind: for people to work
decisions.reason: The word ('avodah) is work or service: the plants are for people to cultivate, or for their use (Genesis 2:15).
Bread (lechem) is often food in general.
Verse 15 names what comes out of the earth, so the verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: וְיַ֤יִן׀יְשַׂמַּ֬ח לְֽבַב־אֱנ֗וֹשׁ לְהַצְהִ֣יל פָּנִ֣ים מִשָּׁ֑מֶן וְ֝לֶ֗חֶם לְֽבַב־אֱנ֥וֹשׁ יִסְעָֽד׃
records.gloss: and wine [that] gladdens [the] heart of humankind, to make [the] face shine with oil, and bread [that] sustains [the] heart of humankind.
pieces: wine that brings joy to human hearts, oil that makes faces glow, and bread that keeps people strong.

L.15: and wine [that] gladdens the heart of humankind, to make [the] face shine with oil, and bread [that] strengthens the heart of humankind.

R.15: He gives wine that makes people happy, olive oil that makes their faces shine, and bread that gives them strength.

decisions.choice: a face shining with oil: festive joy
decisions.reason: Olive oil on the head and face was a sign of gladness and refreshment at a feast (23:5; 45:8). Wine, oil and bread were the main gifts of the land.
To sustain the heart (sa'ad lev) is to refresh someone with food (Genesis 18:5).
Readable starts a new sentence here and supplies its subject.

records.source: יִ֭שְׂבְּעוּ עֲצֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אַֽרְזֵ֥י לְ֝בָנ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָטָֽע׃
records.gloss: [The] trees of YHWH are satisfied, [the] cedars of Lebanon which he planted,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s trees have all the water they need, the cedars {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planted on Lebanon,

L.16: The trees of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are satisfied, the cedars of Lebanon that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planted,

R.16: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gives plenty of water to the great trees {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planted, the cedars of Lebanon.

decisions.choice: the trees of the LORD: the great trees he planted
decisions.reason: These are the great forest trees no one planted but God. Naming God can also mean "great, mighty" (36:7; 80:11).
The cedars of the Lebanon mountains were the tallest and finest trees Israel knew (29:5; 92:13).
Verse 17 goes on to describe these trees, so the verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֭ם צִפֳּרִ֣ים יְקַנֵּ֑נוּ חֲ֝סִידָ֗ה בְּרוֹשִׁ֥ים בֵּיתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: where there birds make nests; [the] stork — fir trees [are] its home.
pieces: where birds build their nests, and the stork lives high in the cypress trees.

L.17: where there birds make nests; the stork — fir trees [are] its home.

R.17: Birds build nests in them. Storks live in the tall cypress trees.

decisions.reason: The bird (chasidah) is an unclean bird (Leviticus 11:19), most likely the stork, which nests in tall trees.
The tree (berosh) is a tall evergreen of the Lebanon; it cannot be named for certain.

records.source: הָרִ֣ים הַ֭גְּבֹהִים לַיְּעֵלִ֑ים סְ֝לָעִ֗ים מַחְסֶ֥ה לַֽשְׁפַנִּֽים׃
records.gloss: The mountains, the high [ones], [are] for the wild goats; crags [are] a refuge for the hyraxes.
pieces: The wild goats have the high mountains, and the hyraxes take shelter in the crags.

L.18: The mountains, the high [ones], [are] for the wild goats; [the] crags [are] a refuge for the hyraxes.

R.18: Wild goats live high up in the mountains. Small animals called rock badgers hide among the rocks.

decisions.reason: The animal (ya'el) is the ibex, a wild goat of the high rocks (Job 39:1).

decisions.choice: hyraxes: small animals of the rocks
decisions.reason: The animal (shafan) is the rock hyrax, a small furry animal that lives among rocks (Proverbs 30:26).
Readable uses a familiar name and says what kind of animal it is.

records.source: עָשָׂ֣ה יָ֭רֵחַ לְמוֹעֲדִ֑ים שֶׁ֝֗מֶשׁ יָדַ֥ע מְבוֹאֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: He made [the] moon for appointed times; [the] sun knows its going down.
pieces: He made the moon for keeping the feasts and seasons; the sun knows the hour it should set.

L.19: He made the moon for appointed times; the sun knows its going down.

R.19: He made the moon to show when the festivals come. The sun knows when it is time to set.

decisions.choice: moon and sun: the fourth day
decisions.reason: God made the lights in the sky "for signs and for appointed times" (Genesis 1:14-16).
The word (mo'adim) is set times, including Israel's festivals, which were fixed by the new moon (81:4).

records.source: תָּֽשֶׁת־חֹ֭שֶׁךְ וִ֣יהִי לָ֑יְלָה בּֽוֹ־תִ֝רְמֹ֗שׂ כָּל־חַיְתוֹ־יָֽעַר׃
records.gloss: You make darkness and it is night; in it every animal of [the] forest creeps about.
pieces: You send darkness, night comes, and every animal of the woods steals out.

L.20: You make darkness, and it becomes night; in it every animal of the forest creeps about.

R.20: You make it dark, and night comes. Then all the animals in the forest come out and move about.

decisions.reason: Night too is God's work and serves his creatures (74:16); the darkness is not a power against him.

records.source: הַ֭כְּפִירִים שֹׁאֲגִ֣ים לַטָּ֑רֶף וּלְבַקֵּ֖שׁ מֵאֵ֣ל אָכְלָֽם׃
records.gloss: The young lions [are] roaring for the prey, and to seek from God their food.
pieces: The young lions roar as they hunt, asking God for their meal.

L.21: The young lions roar for the prey, and to seek their food from God.

R.21: The young lions roar as they hunt. They are asking God for food.

decisions.reason: Even the lion's roar is pictured as a prayer: the hunting animals depend on God for their food (verse 27; Job 38:39-41).

decisions.choice: young lions: lions in their strength
decisions.reason: The word (kefir) is a young lion old enough to hunt (34:11).

records.source: תִּזְרַ֣ח הַ֭שֶּׁמֶשׁ יֵאָסֵפ֑וּן וְאֶל־מְ֝עוֹנֹתָ֗ם יִרְבָּצֽוּן׃
records.gloss: The sun rises; they withdraw, and in their dens they lie down.
pieces: At sunrise they draw back together and settle down to rest in their lairs.

L.22: The sun rises; they withdraw, and in their dens they lie down.

R.22: When the sun comes up, they go back home and sleep in their dens.

decisions.choice: they withdraw: they gather themselves in
decisions.reason: The verb ('asaf, here passive) means to be gathered in, to draw back.

records.source: יֵצֵ֣א אָדָ֣ם לְפָעֳל֑וֹ וְֽלַעֲבֹ֖דָת֣וֹ עֲדֵי־עָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: Humankind goes out to his work and to his labor until evening.
pieces: Then human beings head out to their work and keep at their tasks till evening.

L.23: {{gender:A person|Man}} goes out to {{gender:their|his}} work and to {{gender:their|his}} labor until evening.

R.23: Then people go out to work. They do their jobs until the evening.

decisions.reason: The word ('adam) means human beings; the singular "his" refers to any person.

decisions.choice: the day for people, the night for animals
decisions.reason: When the animals go to their dens (verse 22), people go out; each has its time in God's order.

decisions.choice: A person, their (with "Man", "his" as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: The word means any human being (m1), so Literal gives inclusive wording by default with the traditional words as the alternative; Balanced and Readable say "human beings" and "people".
Balanced and Readable make the link with verse 22 clear (m2).

records.source: מָֽה־רַבּ֬וּ מַעֲשֶׂ֨יךָ׀יְֽהוָ֗ה כֻּ֭לָּם בְּחָכְמָ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָ מָלְאָ֥ה הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ קִנְיָנֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: How many are your works, YHWH! All of them in wisdom you have made; full [is] the earth [of] your possessions.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, how many and varied {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works are! You made them all with skill and wisdom; the earth is crowded with what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made.

L.24: How many are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! All of them in wisdom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made; the earth is full of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} possessions.

R.24: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made so many things! You made them all with great wisdom. The earth is full of the creatures {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made.

decisions.reason: Wisdom (chokhmah) includes the skill of a craftsman; God made the world with wisdom (Proverbs 3:19; 8:22-31).

decisions.choice: your possessions: what you have made and own
decisions.reason: The word (qinyan) is what someone has made or acquired; everything on earth is God's because he made it (Genesis 14:19).

decisions.choice: what you have made (B); the creatures you made (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what God's possessions are here (m2).

records.source: זֶ֤ה׀הַיָּ֥ם גָּדוֹל֮ וּרְחַ֪ב יָ֫דָ֥יִם שָֽׁם־רֶ֭מֶשׂ וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר חַיּ֥וֹת קְ֝טַנּ֗וֹת עִם־גְּדֹלֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: This [is] the sea, great and wide of hands; there [are] moving things, and there is no number, living things small with great.
pieces: Look at the sea, so vast and reaching out on every side! It swarms with countless creatures, living things tiny and huge.

L.25: This [is] the sea, great and wide on both hands; there [are] moving things without number, living things small with great.

R.25: Look at the sea! It is so big and wide. It is full of more living things than anyone can count, both small and large.

decisions.choice: wide of hands: stretching out on every side
decisions.reason: "Hands" here are sides; the sea reaches as far as one can see in every direction.

decisions.choice: moving things: the creatures of the fifth day
decisions.reason: The words recall Genesis 1:20-21, where God fills the waters with swarming creatures.

records.source: שָׁ֭ם אֳנִיּ֣וֹת יְהַלֵּכ֑וּן לִ֝וְיָתָ֗ן זֶֽה־יָצַ֥רְתָּ לְשַֽׂחֶק־בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: There ships go about; Leviathan, this [one] you formed to play in it.
pieces: Ships travel across it, and so does Leviathan, the creature {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} shaped to play in its waves.

L.26: There ships go about; Leviathan, this one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} formed to play in it.

R.26: Ships sail on it. The great sea monster Leviathan is there too. You made it to play in the sea.

decisions.reason: Leviathan is a monster of the sea. Elsewhere it stands for chaos and the powers God defeats (74:14; Isaiah 27:1); here it is only one of God's creatures, made to play.

decisions.choice: to play in it: in the sea
decisions.reason: "In it" may be the sea, or the words may mean that God formed Leviathan to play with it, as the book of Job asks whether anyone could play with it as with a bird.
Readable says what Leviathan is (m1).

records.source: כֻּ֭לָּם אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְשַׂבֵּר֑וּן לָתֵ֖ת אָכְלָ֣ם בְּעִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: All of them to you look, to give their food in its time.
pieces: Every one of them waits for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to give them food when it is needed.

L.27: All of them look to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to give [them] their food in its time.

R.27: All these creatures depend on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to feed them when they need it.

decisions.reason: Psalm 145:15 says nearly the same: "the eyes of all look to you".

decisions.choice: look to you: wait with hope
decisions.reason: The verb (sibber) means to wait with hope and expectation.

records.source: תִּתֵּ֣ן לָ֭הֶם יִלְקֹט֑וּן תִּפְתַּ֥ח יָֽ֝דְךָ֗ יִשְׂבְּע֥וּן טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: You give to them; they gather [it]; you open your hand; they are satisfied [with] good.
pieces: You hand it out and they pick it up; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand, and they eat their fill of good things.

L.28: You give to them, they gather [it] up; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand, they are satisfied [with] good.

R.28: You give them food, and they collect it. You open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand, and they have plenty of good things to eat.

decisions.choice: you give, they gather: when you give
decisions.reason: The short clauses set what God does beside what follows from it: when he gives, they gather; when he opens his hand, they are filled.

records.source: תַּסְתִּ֥יר פָּנֶיךָ֮ יִֽבָּהֵ֫ל֥וּן תֹּסֵ֣ף ר֭וּחָם יִגְוָע֑וּן וְֽאֶל־עֲפָרָ֥ם יְשׁוּבֽוּן׃
records.gloss: You hide your face; they are terrified; you gather their breath; they expire, and to their dust they return.
pieces: If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face away, they panic; if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} withdraw their breath, they breathe their last and go back to the dust they came from.

L.29: You hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, they are terrified; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gather in their breath, they breathe their last, and to their dust they return.

R.29: If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn away from them, they are frightened. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} take their breath from them, they die and become dust again.

decisions.choice: hide your face: withdraw your care
decisions.reason: As in 102:3: when God turns his face away, his creatures are left without the life and help he gives.

decisions.choice: their breath: the breath of life
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) is breath, wind and spirit. Here it is the breath of life, which God gives (verse 30) and takes away.

decisions.choice: to their dust they return: Genesis 3:19
decisions.reason: The words recall Genesis 3:19 and 103:14: living things are made of dust and go back to it (Ecclesiastes 12:7).

records.source: תְּשַׁלַּ֣ח ר֭וּחֲךָ יִבָּרֵא֑וּן וּ֝תְחַדֵּ֗שׁ פְּנֵ֣י אֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: You send forth your spirit; they are created, and you renew [the] face of [the] ground.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} send {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} spirit out, they come into being, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make the face of the land new.

L.30: You send forth {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} spirit, they are created, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} renew the face of the ground.

R.30: Then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} send out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} breath of life, and new creatures are made. You make the land fresh and new again.

decisions.reason: The same word (ruach) is "their breath" in verse 29. God's breath gives life to every creature (Genesis 2:7; Job 33:4). Many readers also see here the Spirit of God at work in creation (Genesis 1:2).

decisions.choice: they are created: new life comes
decisions.reason: The verb (bara') is used only of God's creating. Each new generation of creatures is his new work.
Readable says what God's spirit does here, keeping the link with "breath" in verse 29 (m1).

records.source: יְהִ֤י כְב֣וֹד יְהוָ֣ה לְעוֹלָ֑ם יִשְׂמַ֖ח יְהוָ֣ה בְּמַעֲשָֽׂיו׃
records.gloss: May [the] glory of YHWH be forever; may YHWH rejoice in his works,
pieces: Let the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stand forever; let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be glad in the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made,

L.31: May the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be forever; may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} works,

R.31: Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s glory last forever! May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be happy with all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made.

decisions.reason: God saw all he had made and it was very good (Genesis 1:31). The psalmist prays that God will go on delighting in his creation.
Verse 32 describes this God, so the verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: הַמַּבִּ֣יט לָ֭אָרֶץ וַתִּרְעָ֑ד יִגַּ֖ע בֶּהָרִ֣ים וְֽיֶעֱשָֽׁנוּ׃
records.gloss: the [one who] looks at the earth and it trembles; he touches the mountains and they smoke.
pieces: who glances at the earth and it quakes, who touches the mountains and they send up smoke.

L.32: who looks at the earth and it trembles; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touches the mountains and they smoke.

R.32: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looks at the earth, it shakes. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touches the mountains, they pour out smoke.

decisions.reason: When the LORD came down on Mount Sinai, it smoked and shook (Exodus 19:18; 144:5).
The God who delights in his creatures (verse 31) is also the one whose glance makes the earth quake.

records.source: אָשִׁ֣ירָה לַיהוָ֣ה בְּחַיָּ֑י אֲזַמְּרָ֖ה לֵאלֹהַ֣י בְּעוֹדִֽי׃
records.gloss: I will sing to YHWH in my life; I will make music to my God while I [still am].
pieces: All my life long I will sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; while I am still here I will make music to my God.

L.33: I will sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in my life; I will make music to my God while I [still] am.

R.33: My whole life long I will sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will make music for my God for as long as I live.

decisions.choice: while I still am: as long as I exist
decisions.reason: The word ('od) means "still, yet": as long as he is still alive (146:2, where the same line returns).

records.source: יֶעֱרַ֣ב עָלָ֣יו שִׂיחִ֑י אָ֝נֹכִ֗י אֶשְׂמַ֥ח בַּיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: May my musing be pleasing to him; I, I will rejoice in YHWH.
pieces: Let what I ponder bring {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} pleasure; as for me, my joy is in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.34: May my musing be pleasing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; I, I will rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.34: I hope {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is pleased with what I say about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} makes me glad.

decisions.choice: my musing: my song, my thought
decisions.reason: The word (siach) is earnest speech or thought; in 102:1 it is a troubled complaint, here it is this song of praise.
The pronoun is stressed: whatever others do (verse 35), the psalmist's joy is in the LORD.

records.source: יִתַּ֤מּוּ חַטָּאִ֨ים׀מִן־הָאָ֡רֶץ וּרְשָׁעִ֤ים׀ע֤וֹד אֵינָ֗ם בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Let sinners come to an end from the earth, and [the] wicked [be] no more. Bless, my soul, YHWH. Praise Yah.
pieces: Let sinners be wiped out from the earth, and let no wicked people be left. Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

L.35: Let sinners come to an end from the earth, and the wicked [be] no more. Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}.

R.35: May sinners disappear from the earth. May there be no more wicked people. With all that I am, I praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

decisions.reason: The one dark note in the psalm is a prayer that sin and the wicked be removed from God's good world, so that nothing spoils it (5:11; 37:10). It is a prayer to God to act, not a plan of revenge.
The call (hallelu-yah) means "praise Yah"; Yah is the short form of the divine name (102:19). This is the first place in the Psalms where it occurs; it closes many of the psalms that follow.

decisions.choice: the psalm ends as it began
decisions.reason: The call of verse 1 returns, as it does at the end of Psalm 103.

decisions.choice: With all that I am, I praise the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 103:1.
